name: sixteen-byte-vectors-past-byte-32-and-a-constant-struct-copied-to-a-device-buffer
rationale: One thread (DESIGN D220). The uint4 loads of w and src and the stores to out are aligned to 16 and lie at bytes 32 and up of their buffers, so on a device whose offset alignment is 16 the binder's descriptor ranges start 32 bytes in and those leaves sit at a nonzero residual; the struct assignment *(device Rows *)(out + 4) = rows is a 64-byte align-16 memcpy from the constant buffer to out[4..8]. With w.mask = (0x0000ffff, 0xffff0000, 0x00ff00ff, 0xf0f0f0f0), w.bias = (1, 2, 3, 4), src[2] = (0x12345678, 0x9abcdef0, 0x0f1e2d3c, 0x4b5a6978), and src[3] = (0x01010101, 0x02020202, 0x03030303, 0x04040404): out[2] = (src[2] & w.mask) + w.bias = (0x00005679, 0x9abc0002, 0x001e003f, 0x40506074), out[3] = src[3] ^ w.bias = (0x01010100, 0x02020200, 0x03030300, 0x04040400), and out[4 + i] = rows.r[i], rows.r[i] = (0xa0000001 + 0x10000000 i, ..., 0xa0000004 + 0x10000000 i) except rows.r[2] = (0xc0de0001, 0xc0de0002, 0xc0de0003, 0xc0de0004). The selected bytes are out[2] through out[7] (bytes 32 to 127); none is the 0xab fill. The AIR has no loop.

name: blit-a-three-by-two-window-between-two-different-origins
rationale:
air.convert.u.v2i32.s.v2i16 had no authored case; 38 corpus sources sit behind it. The host is a windowed blit: eight threads each read one texel at a source origin plus their own id and write it at a different destination origin plus the same id, under a bound taken from a third field of the same struct.

The three origins are all different and none is zero, so a case that confused any two of them lands on the wrong texel: the source window starts at (1,1) of a 5x3 source and the destination window at (2,1) of a 6x3 destination. The size field is (3,2) against a grid of (4,2), so the guard has to reject the whole x=3 column - six of the eight threads write, and the twelve destination texels the case does not write must keep their poison, which is what makes the guard observable. Every source texel is a distinct dyadic in all four channels, so a transposed or off-by-one coordinate moves a value rather than repeating one.

One honest limit: the symbol under test SIGN-extends the source coordinate from short to int, and the sibling call on the destination coordinate zero-extends it. The two agree on every coordinate a texture can legally be read at, and a coordinate large enough to separate them is out of range for the read, where Metal leaves the result undefined. So this case pins that the conversion happens and feeds the right coordinate; it cannot pin the signedness, and no case on this shape could.

name: linked-single-unit-pad-gradient
rationale: A 1x1 grid, unit widths, unit source and destination extents, unit divisors, and zero padding bound every dimension loop to one iteration. The exact secondary prefix returns zero and the overwrite specialization selects the exact primary postfix, which writes zero to the sole poisoned destination element.

name: contend-four-device-address-slots
rationale: A CONTENDED read-modify-write on a FLOAT device slot, through a device pointer parked in a local struct field and read back by an out-of-line helper. The integer-atomic-over-a-float-slot is what selects the physical-address model -- Logical SPIR-V cannot retype a logical pointer -- so the atomic lands on an OpConvertUToPtr PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer. This differs from land-a-device-address-field-atomic in the two ways that decide an atomic's SCOPE: the operation is a read-modify-write rather than a compare-exchange, and all four threadgroups target the SAME four words, so an atomic that is atomic only within one threadgroup loses updates. Each of the 256 threads adds 1 to the slot named by gid % 4. A contended add's per-thread RESULT is order-dependent and is not compared; the four accumulators are exact. The slots start at 0.0f, whose bits are zero, so the final bits ARE the count and each slot must read 64.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirteen

name: bicubic-sample-forms-and-texture-types-on-rgba16-float
rationale: Which sample forms and texture types Metal's filter::bicubic applies to, on rgba16_float. The front end admits a bicubic sampler only with both filters bicubic and no mip filter, so the level of detail should select neither a level nor a filter. On one-level textures holding the impulses of bicubic-impulse-weights-per-bound-format (channel c of texel (x, y) is 1 where (x - y - c) mod 4 == 0), each lane samples the 16x16 2D texture implicitly, at level(0), at level(2.5), with bias(2.5), with gradients of half the texture per pixel, and with bias(-2.5) (not min_lod_clamp: Apple's device compiler fails to build a pipeline that samples a bicubic sampler with it); the 16x16x2 array's layer 1 (layer 0 holds 0.25 everywhere, so a wrong layer shows) implicitly and at level(0); the 16-texel 1D texture (channel c is 1 where x mod 4 == c); and the 2D texture with a constant texel offset of (1, -1). Lanes take horizontal fractions k/16 at base texel 4 over rows 4-7 (vertical fraction 0); lane i writes out[10i..10i+9] of buffer 1 in that order. The AIR has no loop.

name: erode-a-uint-texture-through-a-nested-loop-with-two-early-exits
rationale:
The device evidence for `native/cfg/blocks.rs`, which carries the largest absolute gap in the lowering-rule coverage queue at 44 of 112 reached functions with no authored case. Every authored case before this one is a straight-line or single-loop module, so the structurizer's merge inference ran on none of them. An eprintln on each uncovered function in the twelve densest files, swept over all 14,579 sources, mapped every rule to its hosts; 44 uncased modules reach `infer_loop_exit`, `natural_loop_nodes` and `infer_continue_target`, and this is the smallest at 158 lines. Measured with covgain against every cased corpus source plus every public fixture: **42 functions no cased source reaches** -- 29 in `cfg/blocks.rs`, 4 each in `native/reloop_nest/emit.rs` and `verify.rs`, plus `structured_emit/phi_util.rs` and `structured_emit/rewrite.rs`. That is the largest single gain of any candidate measured.

The CFG is what earns it: a bounds guard, an early write-and-return, a four-way border test, then a nested pair of loops over a 3x3 neighbourhood whose inner body can break out of BOTH loops through a shared continuation that carries a two-valued phi, and a final tail that writes only on one of the three ways the region can be left. Five write sites, four of them exclusive.

The kernel is a morphological erosion of a uint texture: a pixel survives as 255 only if it and all eight of its neighbours are nonzero. The texture is 10x10 but the size buffer says 8x8, so the 36 texels outside the logical extent are never dispatched and must keep the 0x11111111 fill -- and every one of them is ZERO in the input, so a scan that reaches past the logical size, or a dispatch that ignores the guard, turns a surviving pixel into a 0 or eats the fill. Every 'on' texel carries a distinct value, so nothing is confusable with a neighbour.

Three zeros at (3,2), (5,5) and (6,1) leave 14 survivors against 50 zeroed pixels, and the resulting map is NOT symmetric about the diagonal, so a transposed neighbourhood offset moves it. One lost inner iteration, one lost outer iteration, and a break that escapes only the inner loop each produce a different map again. The loops are bounded by the literal 3x3 window around a guarded interior pixel, hence `authored_bounded`.

name: read-compare-and-gather-two-depth-array-slices
rationale: Six uncovered depth2d_array families in one kernel -- air.read_depth_2d_array.i16.f32 (2 case-less corpus sources), air.sample_compare_depth_2d_array.f32 (2), air.gather_depth_2d_array.v4f32 (2), air.get_width_depth_2d_array (2) and air.get_height_depth_2d_array (2), 10 sources. Every one carries an array slice operand the non-array form does not, and in all three texel-fetching calls it sits beside another scalar: the read puts it between the coordinate and the offset, sample_compare between the coordinate and the compare reference, and gather between the coordinate and the has-offset flag. The two slices hold the same eight 32nds in two different orders, so no texel value occurs twice in the texture and a lowering that dropped the slice or read its neighbour still fetches a real texel but never the right one. read is asked at both slices of one ushort2 coordinate; sample_compare is asked at both slices of one texel centre with references permuted differently from the slices, so the pass patterns differ between them; gather is asked exactly on an interior texel corner, so its four distinct components pin the component order as well as the slice. The queries answer 4 and 2.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-six-threadgroup-primary

name: read-every-slice-of-one-volume-to-the-same-ushort-texel
rationale: The fragment scales its varying by the volume's own width, height and depth to build a three-component integer coordinate, reads one texel of a texture3d<ushort>, and splits the green channel's two bytes into the low and high halves of the result. Every texel of the volume carries the same four ushorts, so no coordinate the varying can produce changes what is read, and the single-pixel render target captures the byte split, the unsigned red-to-float conversion and the constant alpha exactly.

name: array-texture-write-lands-at-one-texel
rationale: Fifteen air.* texture symbols the corpus reaches once or twice each and that no authored case covered: air.read_texture_2d_ms.v4f16, air.read_texture_2d_ms_array.v4f32, air.read_texture_2d_ms_array.u.v4i16, air.read_texture_2d_array.u.v4i16, air.gather_texture_2d.s.v4i32, air.gather_texture_2d.s.v4i16, air.gather_texture_2d.u.v4i16, air.gather_texture_2d_array.s.v4i32, air.sample_texture_3d.u.v4i32, air.sample_texture_3d.s.v4i32, air.sample_texture_2d.s.v4i16, air.read_texture_buffer_1d.v4f16, air.write_texture_buffer_1d.v4f16, air.write_texture_2d_array.i16.s.v4i32 and air.fence_texture_2d. Every texel is a distinct small integer, exact in half, in float and in both 16- and 32-bit integers, so no row depends on a rounding mode and what the case sees is a wrong TEXEL, SAMPLE or LAYER: each value encodes its own address, with layer, row, column, sample index and component each contributing a different digit. The sampler is a constexpr filter::nearest one, both because the integer formats here cannot be filtered and because it keeps sampler state out of the case. The gather and sample coordinate is 0.5625, which is 2.25 texels into a four-wide texture: sample lands on column 2 with no tie to break and the gather footprint brackets columns 1 and 2 at weight 0.75, again with no tie. Each of the four gather rows reads a different component of the result, which pins Metal's (x0,y1), (x1,y1), (x1,y0), (x0,y0) order rather than only the footprint. The read_write texture is why fence_texture_2d is here: the thread writes it, fences, and reads its own write back, which is exactly what the fence orders. This case observes the array-texture write instead: only the texel at (1, 0) of layer 0 is written, so the other three must still hold the poison the case supplied, and the written texel pins the ushort coordinate operand.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seventeen-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 17 and receives exact float4 zero from all sixteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A nineteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: compare-through-a-comparison-sampler-held-beside-its-depth-texture-in-an-argument-buffer
rationale: DESIGN D285.19: constant argument buffer 0 is DepthMaterial {depth2d<float> d; sampler s;}, and the sampler is the case's own comparison sampler state (normalized, linear, clamp to edge, compareFunction less), which the Metal oracle encodes into field 8 and the engine reads through its comparison sampler array. Thread g compares d at (0.25g, 0.25g), level 0, against 0.5 through m.s and writes the float to buffer 1. Each row of d is (0.25, 0.75), so column 1 passes (0.5 < 0.75) and column 0 fails. In texel space the coordinate is 0.5g - 0.5: g = 0 clamps to texel (0, 0), g = 1 is its center, g = 2 is the midpoint of all four texels (weights 1/4 each), and g = 3 is the center of (1, 1). Every filter weight is 0, 1/4, 1/2 or 1, exact at any subtexel precision, so buffer 1 holds exactly 0, 0, 0.5, 1. A sampler without the case's comparison function (Metal's default, never) gives 0 everywhere.

name: sample-an-unsigned-texture-through-a-sampler-held-beside-it-in-an-argument-buffer
rationale: DESIGN D285.19: constant argument buffer 0 is CountMaterial {texture2d<uint> t; sampler s;}, and the sampler is the case's own sampler state (normalized, nearest, clamp to edge), which the Metal oracle encodes into field 8 and the engine reads through its integer sampler array. Thread g samples t at (0.25g + 0.125, 0.25g + 0.125), level 0, through m.s and writes the uint4 to buffer 1. t is 2x2 rgba32_uint with texel (x, y) = (x + 2y, 10 + x, 20 + y, 7); nearest filtering reads texel floor(2(0.25g + 0.125)) on both axes, never on an edge: (0, 0) for g = 0 and 1, (1, 1) for g = 2 and 3. Buffer 1 holds (0, 10, 20, 7) twice, then (3, 11, 21, 7) twice.

name: sample-in-a-fragment-through-a-sampler-held-beside-its-texture-in-an-argument-buffer
rationale: DESIGN D285.19: the fragment function's constant argument buffer 0 is Material {texture2d<float> t; sampler s;}, and the sampler is the case's own sampler state (normalized, nearest, clamp to edge), which the Metal oracle encodes into field 8 of the fragment stage's buffer and the engine's render executor lists among the draw's argument samplers. The fragment returns t.sample(m.s, in.uv), an implicit-LOD sample, into a 2x2 rgba32_float target. The generated passthrough vertex draws the fullscreen triangle with uv = (ndc + 1) / 2, so each pixel center has uv 0.25 or 0.75 on each axis, the center of one texel of the 2x2 texture, and uv moves by one texel per pixel: level 0 (the texture's only one, the sampler has no mips), read without filtering. t holds texel (x, y) = (1 + x + 2y, 10x, 100y, 1). Metal's target origin is the top left with NDC y up, so target pixel (px, py) reads texel (px, 1 - py): row 0 holds (3, 0, 100, 1), (4, 10, 100, 1) and row 1 holds (1, 0, 0, 1), (2, 10, 0, 1), every value exact in binary32 and distinct per pixel.

name: sample-through-a-linear-sampler-held-beside-its-texture-in-an-argument-buffer
rationale: DESIGN D285.19: constant argument buffer 0 is Material {texture2d<float> t; sampler s;}, and the sampler is the case's own sampler state (normalized, linear, clamp to edge), which the Metal oracle encodes into field 8 and the engine finds through its sampler table. Thread g samples t at (0.25g + 0.125, 0.25g + 0.125), level 0, through m.s and writes the float4 to buffer 1. t is 2x2 rgba16_float with texel (x, y) = (16(x + 2y), 16x, 16y, 16), a linear function of the texel, so a bilinear sample is that function at the texel-space point 0.5g - 0.25 on both axes, clamped to [0, 1]: g = 0 clamps to texel (0, 0); g = 1 and 2 weigh their two texels 3/4 and 1/4 on each axis, exact at any subtexel precision; g = 3 clamps to (1, 1). Buffer 1 holds (0, 0, 0, 16), (12, 4, 4, 16), (36, 12, 12, 16), (48, 16, 16, 16), every value exact in half and float. A nearest or a missing sampler gives other bytes.

name: sample-through-a-pixel-coordinate-sampler-held-in-an-argument-buffer-on-texel-edges
rationale: DESIGN D285.19: constant argument buffer 0 is Material {texture2d<float> t; sampler s;}, and the sampler is the case's own sampler state with pixel coordinates (nearest, clamp to edge), which the Metal oracle encodes into field 8. Thread g samples t at pixel coordinate (0.25g, 0.25g), level 0, through m.s and writes the float4 to buffer 1. t is 6x6 rgba32_float with texel (x, y) = (x + 6y, x, y, 1). Metal reads texel floor(0.25g) on both axes, so threads 4k to 4k + 3 write (7k, k, k, 1) for k = 0 to 5; threads 4k sample exactly on the texel edge k. The engine knows the sampler's coordinate mode only at run time, through the handle's pixel-coordinate flag, and divides the coordinate by the texture's level-0 size (the recorded PixelSamplerScaling near-equivalent): k / 6 rounds up in binary32 for k = 1, 2 and 4 and is exact for k = 3, but 5 / 6 rounds down, so thread 20's scaled coordinate times 6 is exactly 5 - 2^-23, which a binary32 multiply rounds back to the edge 5 and a texel addressing that keeps more precision, truncates, or divides less exactly (Vulkan bounds the division at 2.5 ULP) does not. Thread 20 is the case's probe of whether the near-equivalent answers Metal on a device.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-any
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.

name: linked-single-long-write
rationale: One dispatched invocation addresses one NDArray element. The reference-size and coordinate-mapping constants bound every dimension and stride to one; the linked prefix returns an exact nonzero value, the linked postfix writes it, and both callbacks are loop-free. Transpose variants use one initialized lane and the exact reflected dynamic threadgroup allocation.

name: encode-compute-commands-beside-output
rationale: Each of four threads encodes command tid (kernel buffer 0, a 16-byte threadgroup length, a threadgroup dispatch, a barrier) inside the descriptor's policy, then writes data[tid] * 3 + 7 = 10, 13, 16, 19. The encoded commands are unobserved (no Metal readback; replay owed); the output buffer is the observation.

name: indexed-draws-a-kernel-and-the-host-encode
rationale: Indexed draws in an indirect command buffer that allows indexed draws alone (DESIGN D336), each run by the render template (token 1, inherited from the execution): out[16 * iid + vid] = params[0] * (vid + 1) + params[1] + 1000 * iid, vid the index plus the base vertex and iid counting from the base instance. The host encodes each command's vertex buffers, params and out windows at 256 * t bytes, and command 2's draw: 4 32-bit indices from byte 4 of buffer 2 (0, 11, 2, 9), base vertex 1, one instance from 1. Producer thread 0 encodes command 0's draw of 5 16-bit device indices from the second of buffer 1 (2, 7, 3, 5, 11), base vertex -2, two instances from 1; thread 1 command 1's draw of 3 32-bit constant indices of buffer 2 (6, 0, 11), base vertex 4, one instance. Window 0 (scale 3, bias 20) holds 1023, 1026, 1032, 1038, 1050 at words 16, 17, 19, 21, 25 and 2023, 2026, 2032, 2038, 2050 at words 32, 33, 35, 37, 41; window 1 (scale 7, bias 1) 36, 78, 113 at words 68, 74, 79; window 2 (scale 5, bias 100) 1110, 1120, 1155, 1165 at words 145, 147, 154, 156. Every other word keeps the 0xab fill, and every written byte differs from it.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fifteen-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 15 and receives exact float4 zero from all fourteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A seventeen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: average-five-texels-across-two-lanes-without-a-reciprocal
rationale: Two threads stride a five-wide row by two, so one covers three texels and the other two, and the sixth coordinate falls outside the width and is dropped -- which makes the shared count five, an odd divisor, rather than a power of two. Each finalizing thread reduces one component across both scratch entries and writes its own lane, so all six floats are observed. Every channel is a small multiple of one over a thousand and twenty-four, so each partial sum is exact and only the final divide can round; both component sums are chosen so the correctly rounded quotient and a multiply by the rounded reciprocal are different floats, and the divide carries no `arcp`, so the exact quotient is the only answer allowed.

name: clear-both-layers-at-the-slice-the-grid-selects
rationale: Two invocations differing only in thread_position_in_grid.z each write the same constant float4 to the array slice their own z names. Both slices start poisoned and the captured region spans both, so a lowering that drops the layer operand or clamps it to zero leaves slice one unwritten.

name: custom-callback-zero-state
rationale: A zero shader-state vector disables every optional texture, table, framebuffer-fetch, and dithering branch. The separately linked visible callback returns its incoming half4 unchanged, while zeroed mandatory globals and custom arguments keep every reachable access in bounds. The poisoned one-pixel half4 render target observes the exact linked fragment result.

name: both-tanh-halves-saturate-to-one
rationale:
One invocation at gid (0, 0). Both ratio buffers are authored non-zero (3 and 5) but are multiplied by the converted gid, which is zero, so both sample coordinates are exactly (0.5, 0.5) -- the centre of a one-texel texture, which is the same texel whatever the module's static sampler filters with. That removes every source of inexactness ahead of the two air.tanh.f16 calls.
Both calls are then driven deep into saturation, which is the only place a half transcendental is byte-authorable: in binary16 tanh rounds to exactly 1.0 once 1 - tanh(x) falls below 2^-12, past about 4.51. Channel 1 of both low-resolution maps is authored -1, so their sum is -2 and the first argument is (0.19995 + 2) * 28, about 61.6 -- more than thirteen times the threshold. The flow texel is zero, so its dot product and square root are exactly zero and the second argument is 28 exactly. Both tanh results are therefore exactly 1, both blends are exactly 1, and the written half is 1 in all four channels.
A tanh that stops short of one on either call moves the product, and so does a lowering that reads the wrong channel of either map, swaps the two maps' roles with the flow texture, or drops the square root: all of those change at least one argument by far more than the saturation margin.

name: fast-math-functions-beside-their-compositions
rationale: Each of 1024 threads writes 24 words for its (x, y): fast tan, sin, cos, and 1 / cos; x / y, 1 / y, fast sqrt, and fast rsqrt; fast exp2, log2, exp, and log; fast pow(x, y), exp2(y * log2 x), fast powr(x, y), and fast fmod(x, y); fast tanh, atan, and asin, and exp2(x * log2 e); trunc(x / y), log2 x * ln 2, x * rsqrt x, and sin x * (1 / cos x). Every fast function stands beside the composition MSL Table 8.2 gives for it or a candidate one, over the same operands, compiled with the default fast math. Operands: 256 in [-pi, pi] with exponents in [-16, 16], 128 small, 96 past pi up to 2^24, 32 huge, 256 positive over the whole range, 128 divisors from the denormals past 2^126, 64 near 1, and 64 pairs of special values. Question (WP-FMX, DESIGN D253): where is Apple's fast result a deterministic composition of operations a device does exactly (which the translation can then emit), and where does it rest on Apple's own approximations (the residue).

name: clear-counter-word
rationale: The loop-free entry unconditionally stores aligned uint value zero to its sole four-byte read/write buffer; one invocation changes every poisoned output byte.

name: linked-k48-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-float-64-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48 (one whole 32-deep block, the unsafe loader, and a 16-deep remainder, the safe one). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 32 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (expert strides w, scales and biases batch stride = N*K = 3072), writing only its own rows. W[e][k][n] (w_ld = 64 bytes): both experts hold q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads); expert 0's scales repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and expert 1's are half of them (biases unread without the bias bit). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . W/2 = a . W): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Each dequantized weight is a multiple of 0.25 at most 30, exact in float, and each x at most 10; each product with x a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-float-64-non-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The non-transposed float 64 counterpart of the committed mps_gather_qmm_rhs_t_bfloat_64 case (DESIGN D272): mps_gather_qmm_rhs_n_float_64 with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.
